title: The Best Years of Your Life

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: In one of the movie versions of the Oscar Wilde novel, The Picture of Dorian Gray,
sentences.zh: 在奥斯卡·王尔德小说《道林·格雷的画像》的某个电影版本中，

sentences.en: the actor Hurd Hatfield stares longingly at a painting of himself.
sentences.zh: 演员赫德·哈特菲尔德深情地凝视着一幅自己的肖像画。

sentences.en: The picture shows a young man bursting with health and vitality.
sentences.zh: 画中是一个充满健康与活力的年轻人。

sentences.en: As Dorian Gray reflects on how he is going to change with age,
sentences.zh: 当道林·格雷想到自己会随着年龄增长而改变，

sentences.en: while his picture will stay the same, a strange wish passes through his head.
sentences.zh: 而画像却能保持原样时，一个奇怪的念头闪过他的脑海。

sentences.en: And I could be always what I am now.
sentences.zh: 如果我能永远保持现在的样子，

sentences.en: For that, I would give everything.
sentences.zh: 为此，我愿意付出一切。

sentences.en: There's nothing in the whole world I would not give.
sentences.zh: 这世上没有什么是我不愿给的。

sentences.en: I would give my soul for that.
sentences.zh: 我愿意为此出卖灵魂。

sentences.en: In the story, Dorian Gray makes a pact with the devil.
sentences.zh: 在故事里，道林·格雷与魔鬼做了交易。

sentences.en: The painting starts to age in his place.
sentences.zh: 画像开始代替他衰老。

sentences.en: The physical degradation of the picture isn't only about the passing years.
sentences.zh: 画像的生理退化不仅仅是因为岁月的流逝。

sentences.en: The picture takes on the corruption of the character's many misdeeds.
sentences.zh: 画像承载了这个角色种种恶行带来的腐化。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Dorian Gray himself stays eternally youthful.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，道林·格雷本人却永葆青春。

sentences.en: Oscar Wilde wrote the story in the late 19th century.
sentences.zh: 奥斯卡·王尔德在19世纪末写下了这个故事。

sentences.en: The movie came out in the middle of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 这部电影在20世纪中叶上映。

sentences.en: The 21st century is not that different in its preoccupations from its predecessors.
sentences.zh: 21世纪人们的忧虑与前人并无太大不同。

sentences.en: Movies, TV shows, and the fashion industry still worship at the altar of youth.
sentences.zh: 电影、电视节目和时尚产业依然在崇拜青春的祭坛。

sentences.en: People around the world spend billions of dollars on potions and injections and surgical interventions to keep the signs of age at bay.
sentences.zh: 世界各地的人们花费数十亿美元购买药水、注射剂和进行外科手术，以抵御衰老的迹象。

sentences.en: Clickbait ads on many websites show you what the youthful stars of yesteryears look like today.
sentences.zh: 许多网站上的诱饵广告向你展示昔日的青春偶像如今的模样。

sentences.en: The message couldn't be clearer.
sentences.zh: 信息再明确不过了。

sentences.en: Aging is a terrible thing.
sentences.zh: 衰老是一件可怕的事情。

sentences.en: Growing old is a horror show.
sentences.zh: 变老是一场恐怖秀。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, astonishing new research about aging that could change the way everyone thinks about life.
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》，我们将探讨关于衰老的惊人新研究，这可能会改变每个人对生命的看法。

sentences.en: If you're short, you don't know what it feels like to be tall.
sentences.zh: 如果你个子矮，你就不知道长得高是什么感觉。

sentences.en: If you're white, you won't know what it's like to be black.
sentences.zh: 如果你是白人，你就不会知道身为黑人是什么体验。

sentences.en: Lots of aspects of identity are like this.
sentences.zh: 身份的许多方面都是如此。

sentences.en: They are fixed.
sentences.zh: 它们是固定的。

sentences.en: But there is one form of identity that is certain to change with time.
sentences.zh: 但有一种身份注定会随着时间而改变。

sentences.en: Young people today will become old people tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 今天的年轻人明天就会变成老人。

sentences.en: But while growing old is inevitable, it comes with so much psychological and cultural baggage that lots of us avoid thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 虽然变老不可避免，但它伴随着太多的心理和文化包袱，以至于我们许多人都不愿去想它。

sentences.en: In popular culture, getting old means getting kicked out.
sentences.zh: 在流行文化中，变老意味着被淘汰。

sentences.en: Lots of elderly people discover that aging makes them invisible to others.
sentences.zh: 许多老年人发现，衰老让他们在他人眼中变得隐形。

sentences.en: At Stanford University, psychologist Laura Carstensen has focused her attention on the topic of aging.
sentences.zh: 在斯坦福大学，心理学家劳拉·卡斯滕森一直专注于衰老这一课题。

sentences.en: She has discovered some astonishing things.
sentences.zh: 她发现了一些惊人的事实。

sentences.en: Laura Carstensen, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 劳拉·卡斯滕森，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Pleasure to be with you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能和你在一起。

sentences.en: Laura, I want to take you back to 1974 when you were 21 years old.
sentences.zh: 劳拉，我想带你回到1974年，那时你21岁。

sentences.en: Like many young people on the cusp of adulthood, you didn't give much thought to aging.
sentences.zh: 像许多处于成年边缘的年轻人一样，你当时并没有过多考虑衰老的问题。

sentences.en: What would you say your priorities were at this time of your life?
sentences.zh: 你觉得当时你人生中的首要任务是什么？

sentences.en: My priorities were dating, exploring, and thinking about future jobs and possibilities
sentences.zh: 我的首要任务是约会、探索，思考未来的工作和可能性，

sentences.en: and where I would live and what I was going to do the next day, the next week, the next year.
sentences.zh: 以及我住在哪里，明天、下周、明年要做什么。

sentences.en: I thought a lot about my future.
sentences.zh: 我思考了很多关于未来的事情。

sentences.en: I didn't think at all about aging.
sentences.zh: 我完全没有考虑过衰老。

sentences.en: Your life changed very dramatically one night that year.
sentences.zh: 那年的一天晚上，你的人生发生了巨大的改变。

sentences.en: Laura, I understand that you and some friends were going to a concert.
sentences.zh: 劳拉，我听说你和朋友们当时正要去参加一场音乐会。

sentences.en: Tell me what happened, Laura.
sentences.zh: 告诉我发生了什么，劳拉。

sentences.en: Yeah, I worked as a waitress in a restaurant, and a bunch of us, after closing, decided we would go to a concert.
sentences.zh: 是的，我当时在一家餐馆做服务员，下班后我们一群人决定去听音乐会。

sentences.en: It was about an hour outside of town, and we divided up into cars, drove out, and we went to this concert.
sentences.zh: 地点在城外大约一小时车程的地方，我们分乘几辆车开了过去，参加了那场音乐会。

sentences.en: At the end of the evening, we said, well, let's go back and play some pool.
sentences.zh: 晚上结束时，我们说，好吧，我们回去打台球吧。

sentences.en: So we divided up again into different cars and started to head back to town.
sentences.zh: 于是我们又分乘不同的车，开始往城里赶。

sentences.en: I happened to get in the car with a man I hardly knew who was very drunk, and I caught on to that pretty quickly and asked him to stop.
sentences.zh: 我恰好坐进了一个我不怎么认识的男人的车里，他喝得很醉，我很快就察觉到了，并让他停车。

sentences.en: I remember putting my hand out on the dashboard as he was going ever faster,
sentences.zh: 我记得当他越开越快时，我把手伸向了仪表盘，

sentences.en: and that was the last thing I remembered before waking up in a ditch on the side of the road.
sentences.zh: 那是我醒来躺在路边的沟里之前记得的最后一件事。

sentences.en: He drove off the road and rolled down an embankment.
sentences.zh: 他把车开出了路面，翻下了路堤。

sentences.en: The car turned two or three times over, and I broke about 20-plus bones, but my left leg was injured most badly.
sentences.zh: 车子翻滚了两三次，我断了20多根骨头，但左腿伤得最重。

sentences.en: My femur cracked in half, and I had many other fractures through the knee and the ankle.
sentences.zh: 我的股骨断成了两截，膝盖和脚踝还有许多其他骨折。

sentences.en: And I cracked ribs, I had a concussion, lots of facial lacerations, lots and lots of injuries.
sentences.zh: 我还断了肋骨，脑震荡，脸上有很多撕裂伤，伤得非常非常重。

sentences.en: I'm assuming there were a bunch of surgeries that must have followed this and sort of very intense hospitalization here.
sentences.zh: 我猜想这之后一定经历了一连串的手术，还有非常密集的住院治疗。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: For the first couple of weeks, they couldn't do surgery because I had been injured so badly they couldn't give me anesthesia.
sentences.zh: 最初的几周，他们无法进行手术，因为我伤得太重，无法接受麻醉。

sentences.en: So those were the toughest two weeks.
sentences.zh: 所以那是最艰难的两周。

sentences.en: And then they began a surgery, but mostly they just kept my leg hanging in the air.
sentences.zh: 后来他们开始手术，但大部分时间只是把我的腿悬吊在空中。

sentences.en: It's that cartoonish image, you know, you have of someone laying in a hospital bed and the leg is being held upwards, and that would keep it somewhat straight.
sentences.zh: 就是那种卡通式的画面，你知道的，一个人躺在病床上，腿被向上吊着，这样能让它保持平直。

sentences.en: Was there a period in this window, Laura, where people were afraid that you might not make it?
sentences.zh: 劳拉，在那段时间里，有没有人担心你可能挺不过去？

sentences.en: I mean, it sounds like this was a very, very serious crash, and the injuries were really serious.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，听起来这是一场非常非常严重的车祸，伤势真的很严重。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Certainly, there was the expectation that I may not make it.
sentences.zh: 确实有人认为我可能挺不过去了。

sentences.en: I remember at a point during that time, I wished I wouldn't make it.
sentences.zh: 我记得在那段时间的某个时刻，我希望自己挺不过去。

sentences.en: In hindsight, I remember thinking, there are things worse than dying.
sentences.zh: 事后回想起来，我记得当时想，有些事情比死亡更糟糕。

sentences.en: But I kept sort of becoming unconscious, but then coming out of it again in those early days and, you know, eventually started to heal.
sentences.zh: 但在那段早期的日子里，我总是陷入昏迷，然后又清醒过来，你知道的，最终开始康复了。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if your priorities changed around this time.
sentences.zh: 我想知道你当时的优先事项是否发生了改变。

sentences.en: You know, you talked about how your priorities at age 21 were the priorities of anyone who was age 21.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你谈到21岁时的优先事项和任何21岁的人一样。

sentences.en: You're thinking about what's happening next week, next weekend.
sentences.zh: 你在想下周、下周末会发生什么。

sentences.en: You're maybe thinking about your dating life.
sentences.zh: 你可能在想你的约会生活。

sentences.en: You're thinking about your career.
sentences.zh: 你在想你的职业生涯。

sentences.en: How did that worldview change as a result of the crash?
sentences.zh: 那场车祸之后，你的世界观发生了怎样的改变？

sentences.en: I, like many people who have these near-death experiences, completely changed how I thought about life.
sentences.zh: 像许多有过这种濒死体验的人一样，我彻底改变了对生活的看法。

sentences.en: And suddenly, life was something I didn't take for granted anymore.
sentences.zh: 突然间，生活不再是我理所当然拥有的东西了。

sentences.en: And life wasn't to be lived for fun and entertainment and exploration.
sentences.zh: 生活不再是为了享乐、娱乐和探索。

sentences.en: I, for the first time, really saw how valuable time was.
sentences.zh: 我第一次真正看到了时间的宝贵。

sentences.en: Laura's social world changed, too.
sentences.zh: 劳拉的社交圈也发生了变化。

sentences.en: A large circle of acquaintances was replaced by a bright spotlight on a small group of family and close friends.
sentences.zh: 一大群泛泛之交被一小群家人和密友所取代，他们成了我关注的焦点。

sentences.en: And for that, I felt incredible gratitude to be surrounded by people who really cared about me.
sentences.zh: 为此，我感到无比感激，因为我被真正关心我的人包围着。

sentences.en: And my parents came to visit.
sentences.zh: 我的父母来看我了。

sentences.en: My siblings came to visit.
sentences.zh: 我的兄弟姐妹来看我了。

sentences.en: My dad came every day.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸每天都来。

sentences.en: And I don't know what I would have done without that connection to the outside world
sentences.zh: 我不知道如果没有那种与外界的联系，我会怎么办，

sentences.en: and without the knowledge that I was embedded in a group of people who cared.
sentences.zh: 也不知道如果没有那种被一群关心我的人包围的感觉，我会怎样。

sentences.en: Tell me about your recovery.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说你的康复过程。

sentences.en: I understand that you were in the hospital for several months as you were recovering from these injuries.
sentences.zh: 我听说你在医院住了好几个月来治疗这些伤势。

sentences.en: The way I remember this, it was about a month and a half before I thought about much of anything other than my injuries and how badly I had been hurt.
sentences.zh: 据我记忆，在大约一个半月的时间里，我除了伤势和自己伤得有多重之外，几乎什么都没想。

sentences.en: But then I started to kind of wake up, if you will, and I started to get bored.
sentences.zh: 但后来我开始“苏醒”了，如果可以这么说的话，我开始感到无聊。

sentences.en: It's when you lay flat on your back with your leg up in the air, strung up in the air, there's just so much you can do day to day.
sentences.zh: 当你平躺在床上，腿被悬吊在空中时，每天能做的事情实在有限。

sentences.en: And I got really bored.
sentences.zh: 我真的感到非常无聊。

sentences.en: Laura's father, who was a professor, offered her a way out of her boredom.
sentences.zh: 劳拉的父亲是一位教授，他为她提供了一种摆脱无聊的方法。

sentences.en: And he had always wanted me to go to college.
sentences.zh: 他一直希望我去上大学。

sentences.en: I had not gone to college up to that point.
sentences.zh: 在那之前我还没有上过大学。

sentences.en: I was 21 in this accident.
sentences.zh: 我出车祸时21岁。

sentences.en: And he suggested when I complained about being bored that maybe I should take a course.
sentences.zh: 当我抱怨无聊时，他建议我或许可以修一门课程。

sentences.en: And I was kind of resistant to it.
sentences.zh: 我当时有点抵触。

sentences.en: And he said, really, just name a course.
sentences.zh: 他说，真的，随便选一门课就行。

sentences.en: And he would go tape the lectures and bring them to me.
sentences.zh: 他会去录下讲座，然后带给我听。

sentences.en: So I took introductory psychology as a hospital patient, laying flat on my back with my leg tied in the air.
sentences.zh: 于是我作为一名住院病人，平躺在床上，腿被吊在空中，修了心理学入门课。

sentences.en: Wait, so your dad actually sat in the psychology classes and recorded them and brought you back the cassettes to listen to?
sentences.zh: 等等，所以你爸爸真的坐在心理学课堂里录音，然后把磁带带回来给你听？

sentences.en: My dad was a saint.
sentences.zh: 我爸爸是个圣人。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: My dad was a biophysicist, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，我爸爸是位生物物理学家。

sentences.en: And when he first asked me what I wanted to take, I was like saying, oh, not physics.
sentences.zh: 当他第一次问我想修什么课时，我说，哦，别选物理。

sentences.en: And he said, no, anything, anything.
sentences.zh: 他说，没问题，什么都行，什么都行。

sentences.en: And so, yes, he went to every lecture of introductory psychology with a tape recorder and tape recorded the lectures and brought them to me in the hospital.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，他带着录音机去听了每一节心理学入门课，录下讲座，然后带到医院给我。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So while you were in the hospital, the nurses assigned you a task, which was also in some ways perhaps a psychology workshop,
sentences.zh: 所以当你在医院时，护士给你指派了一个任务，在某种程度上也许也是一个心理学研讨会，

sentences.en: of talking with some of the elderly patients who were in the same ward as you.
sentences.zh: 就是和你病房里的几位老年病人交谈。

sentences.en: Why did they ask you to do that, Laura?
sentences.zh: 劳拉，她们为什么要让你做那个？

sentences.en: Well, I had gotten to know the nurses.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我已经和护士们混熟了。

sentences.en: You know, again, you're with the same people day after day.
sentences.zh: 你知道，毕竟你每天都和同样的人在一起。

sentences.en: And so we had begun to talk a little bit and I complained to them about being bored.
sentences.zh: 所以我们开始交谈，我向她们抱怨我很无聊。

sentences.en: And they said, we've got an assignment for you.
sentences.zh: 她们说，我们有个任务交给你。

sentences.en: There are a lot of older women who come into the orthopedic ward and we're going to put them in this room with you.
sentences.zh: 有很多老年妇女住进骨科病房，我们要把她们安排在你这个房间里。

sentences.en: I was on a four bed ward.
sentences.zh: 我住的是四人间。

sentences.en: And your job is to talk to them and keep them alert.
sentences.zh: 你的工作就是和她们聊天，让她们保持清醒。

sentences.en: And so they don't, you know, get confused and so on.
sentences.zh: 这样她们就不会，你知道的，感到困惑之类的。

sentences.en: And so we're giving you that job.
sentences.zh: 所以我们把这个工作交给你。

sentences.en: So two things happened.
sentences.zh: 于是发生了两件事。

sentences.en: One, I'm taking introductory psychology.
sentences.zh: 第一，我在修心理学入门课。

sentences.en: And the second one is I've now been assigned to talk to older women.
sentences.zh: 第二，我现在被指派去和老年妇女交谈。

sentences.en: Now, I can't tell whether this was a psychological intervention to help you or a psychological intervention to help the people you were talking with.
sentences.zh: 现在，我无法判断这到底是帮助你的心理干预，还是帮助你交谈对象的心理干预。

sentences.en: But perhaps it was both at the same time.
sentences.zh: 但也许两者兼而有之。

sentences.en: Well, really, this was about helping me.
sentences.zh: 嗯，实际上，这主要是为了帮助我。

sentences.en: They were trying to give me a gift of a job.
sentences.zh: 她们是想给我一份工作作为礼物。

sentences.en: Is there anything you gleaned from the time you spent with these elderly patients in the ward?
sentences.zh: 你在病房与这些老年病人相处的时间里，有什么收获吗？

sentences.en: So many things.
sentences.zh: 收获太多了。

sentences.en: I learned so much from this experience about aging.
sentences.zh: 我从这次经历中学到了很多关于衰老的知识。

sentences.en: For one, their lives were so different from one another.
sentences.zh: 首先，她们的生活彼此之间截然不同。

sentences.en: And their personalities and their outlooks on life were so different from one another that to the extent that I had stereotypes about what older people were like,
sentences.zh: 她们的个性和人生观也各不相同，以至于我之前对老年人有什么刻板印象的话，

sentences.en: they went quite far in challenging those stereotypes.
sentences.zh: 她们的经历在很大程度上挑战了那些刻板印象。

sentences.en: One woman that I shared a room with was a matriarch of her family.
sentences.zh: 我和其中一位女士同住一个房间，她是她家族的族长。

sentences.en: And these young kids would come in and sit on the bed and talk to her.
sentences.zh: 那些小孩子们会进来坐在床边和她聊天。

sentences.en: There were other women who were really sad, really in a tough situation.
sentences.zh: 还有其他一些女士真的很悲伤，处境非常艰难。

sentences.en: I remember one woman in the hospital room who had to sell her home in order to pay the hospital bill before they would discharge her.
sentences.zh: 我记得病房里有一位女士，为了支付住院费，她不得不卖掉自己的房子才能出院。

sentences.en: And so she had to be transferred to a nursing home instead of back to her own home.
sentences.zh: 所以她不得不被转到疗养院，而不是回到自己的家。

sentences.en: And it was all for financial reasons.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是出于经济原因。

sentences.en: There was another woman who just kind of laid in her bed and stared at the ceiling all day.

sentences.en: There was another insight I had from spending so much time with these older women who were also spending all their days in bed being cared for by other people.
sentences.zh: 我从与这些老年女性相处的漫长时光中，还获得了另一个洞见，她们也整天躺在床上，由他人照料。

sentences.en: And that insight was just how much we had in common.
sentences.zh: 那个洞见就是，我们之间竟然有这么多共同点。

sentences.en: And so I was 21 and these women were, you know, in their 70s and 80s and probably 90s.

sentences.en: But we were all dependent on other people for everything from, you know, being fed to staying clean to having any social interaction.

sentences.en: So suddenly I shared these characteristics that I would have thought of as characteristics of old people or sick people.

sentences.en: But now it was me too.

sentences.en: And so that also changed.

sentences.en: And it made me think about the world and how the world comes to shape who we are.

sentences.en: And the one insight I had about aging, or at least was at the beginnings of my thinking about aging,

sentences.en: And that was the insight that led me to be interested in the science of aging.

sentences.en: When she was a young woman, she sustained some serious injuries in a car crash.

sentences.en: As she recovered in the hospital, she found herself surrounded by elderly patients with many infirmities.

sentences.en: The experience helped her decide to specialize in the science of aging.

sentences.en: Laura, when you started your career as a psychologist in the early 1980s,
sentences.zh: 劳拉，当你在20世纪80年代初开始你的心理学家生涯时，

sentences.en: there was a scientific consensus about what it meant to grow old.
sentences.zh: 科学界对于衰老意味着什么已经达成了共识。

sentences.en: Was it fair to say that that consensus was a grim one?
sentences.zh: 可以说那个共识是相当悲观的吗？

sentences.en: Oh, it was grim indeed.
sentences.zh: 哦，确实非常悲观。

sentences.en: Indeed, aging was considered to be a serious threat to virtually everyone's mental health.
sentences.zh: 事实上，衰老被认为是对几乎所有人心理健康的严重威胁。

sentences.en: There was a clinical psychology textbook that I had when I was in graduate school.
sentences.zh: 我读研究生时有一本临床心理学教科书。

sentences.en: So this was a textbook on psychopathology.
sentences.zh: 那是一本关于精神病理学的教科书。

sentences.en: They had a chapter on anxiety, a chapter on depression, a chapter on drug abuse,
sentences.zh: 里面有关于焦虑的章节，关于抑郁的章节，关于药物滥用的章节，

sentences.en: and then they end a chapter on old age.
sentences.zh: 最后还有一章是关于老年的。

sentences.en: So old age itself was considered pathological.
sentences.zh: 所以，老年本身就被视为一种病态。

sentences.en: And I'm assuming that when scientists were talking about the pathologies of old age,
sentences.zh: 我假设当科学家们谈论衰老的病理时，

sentences.en: they were referring to things like declines in cognitive function, impairments in memory,
sentences.zh: 他们指的是认知功能下降、记忆力受损、

sentences.en: depression, anxiety, a whole range of probleMs.
sentences.zh: 抑郁、焦虑等一系列问题。

sentences.en: The whole range.
sentences.zh: 涵盖了所有这些问题。

sentences.en: And, you know, at the time, people also believed that Alzheimer's disease

sentences.en: was the inevitable consequence of aging.
sentences.zh: 是衰老的必然结果。

sentences.en: So that cognitive impairment would begin and would eventually progress to dementia.

sentences.en: So that that was the fate of people who lived very long lives.
sentences.zh: 这就是长寿之人的宿命。

sentences.en: So soon after you started working as an academic,
sentences.zh: 那么在你开始学术工作后不久，

sentences.en: the National Institute of Mental Health funded a study to assess the prevalence of psychiatric disorders.

sentences.en: What did it find and what was its impact on you, Laura?
sentences.zh: 劳拉，这项研究发现了什么？它对你有什么影响？

sentences.en: Yes, this was an epidemiological catchment area study of mental health conducted in the early 1980s.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是一项在20世纪80年代初进行的关于心理健康的流行病学集水区研究。

sentences.en: And it was not a study designed about old age at all.
sentences.zh: 它根本不是一项专门针对老年的研究。

sentences.en: It was a study that was designed so that the researchers could get a better estimate

sentences.en: of different forms of psychopathology in the community.

sentences.en: And so what they did was to have trained clinicians go out into the communities
sentences.zh: 所以他们所做的是让受过培训的临床医生深入社区，

sentences.en: and interview a representative sample of people
sentences.zh: 并对具有代表性的样本人群进行访谈，

sentences.en: in a number of different geographical areas around the country.
sentences.zh: 这些人群来自全国各地的不同地理区域。

sentences.en: So it was the best epidemiological study of mental health that had been done in this country,
sentences.zh: 所以这是当时在这个国家，甚至可能是在全球范围内，所做过的最好的心理健康流行病学研究。

sentences.en: probably anywhere at the time.

sentences.en: And we began to run a study, which since has become widely replicated, but it was a study where we presented

sentences.en: positive, negative, and neutral stimuli to younger, middle-aged, and older adults.
sentences.zh: 年轻人、中年人和老年人展示了积极、消极和中性的刺激物。

sentences.en: And we had them sit in front of a computer screen and they would go through the images.
sentences.zh: 我们让他们坐在电脑屏幕前，浏览这些图像。

sentences.en: And then after they've done this viewing, tell us all the images you remember.
sentences.zh: 浏览结束后，让他们说出自己记得的所有图像。

sentences.en: And what we find is that younger people remember almost the same numbers of positive and negative images.
sentences.zh: 结果发现，年轻人对积极和消极图像的记忆数量几乎相同。

sentences.en: By middle age, we see a preference and memory for the positive images.
sentences.zh: 到了中年，我们观察到对积极图像的偏好和记忆有所增加。

sentences.en: And in old age, that preference is whopping.
sentences.zh: 而到了老年，这种偏好变得非常显著。

sentences.en: That is, older people are remembering almost exclusively the positive images, and they're not recalling the negative, nor the neutral ones.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，老年人几乎只记得积极的图像，而不会回想起消极或中性的图像。

sentences.en: And so that was the first time we'd seen this.
sentences.zh: 这是我们第一次观察到这种现象。

sentences.en: It was a little surprising to us because we weren't exactly clear why people would selectively attend to positive and not negative, too,

sentences.en: because negative could be emotionally meaningful.

sentences.en: And we thought this was super interesting.
sentences.zh: 我们觉得这非常有意思。

sentences.en: We then ran a study of autobiographical memory, again, same finding, using neuroimaging,
sentences.zh: 随后，我们利用神经影像技术对自传体记忆进行了研究，结果依然相同，

sentences.en: where you look at amygdala activation in response to the negative, the neutral, the positive.
sentences.zh: 即观察杏仁核在面对消极、中性和积极刺激时的激活情况。

sentences.en: And again, what we see is more amygdala activation in response to positive viewing than the viewing of negative images in older people.
sentences.zh: 再次发现，老年人在观看积极图像时，杏仁核的激活程度要高于观看消极图像时。

sentences.en: And again, let me loop this back to some of the thinking about how negative aging was years ago.

sentences.en: Prior to the study we did, and this was a study published in the early 2000s,
sentences.zh: 在我们这项研究（发表于21世纪初）之前，

sentences.zh: 此前只有一项研究观察过杏仁核对情绪刺激的反应，

sentences.en: but the researchers had only used negative stimuli, and older people didn't remember them as well.

sentences.en: But what we showed is the amygdala is activated just fine in response to positive stimuli.

sentences.en: And many people, by the way, think of the amygdala as more of a salience indicator than emotion per se, right?

sentences.en: And since then, as I say, there are now hundreds of studies showing the positivity effect.

sentences.en: However, people, as it turns out, were young college students in virtually all of these studies.
